abstraction_design.rationale: Where the app has real variation (cards, data helpers) the abstractions are well-shaped and stretch nicely; but the resource-detail pages are four structural near-copies with no shared page scaffold, so a new Items section is mostly a copy of moves/[name].js rather than a reuse of it.

findings.issue: The GRACILE_BUILD build-time guard is hand-copied into six route files and its constant is defined in the npm build script (app/package.json:6), with no comment explaining why it exists. A new route that omits it will fetch API data during vite build (Gracile invokes every GET handler once at build time to render premises), and a maintainer who doesn't know that will either delete it or break the build.
findings.suggestion: Extract a single documented helper (e.g. lib/build-mode.js exporting isBuildPass() with a comment citing Gracile's build-time handler invocation), or wrap defineRoute in a shared makeRoute() that applies the guard; set the flag from vite.config.js (define/env) instead of the npm script so the contract lives in one file.

findings.issue: The not-found template fragment is duplicated in five files (moves/[name].js:58, abilities/[name].js:56, types/[name].js:82, pokemon/[name].js:285, 404.js:12) and the not-found catch-block/props in four; types/[name].js even has it twice (:44 and :72).
findings.suggestion: Add notFoundTemplate() and notFoundProps() helpers to lib/components.js (or document.js) and use them from every route, so the wording and status handling change in one place.

findings.issue: The Pokémon route is a ~360-line monolith containing the entire Moves subsystem (STAT_LABELS, METHOD_ORDER, moveTable, loadMoveRows, sortMoveRows) plus evolution rendering — the framework's docs recommend routes stay thin entry points, and the empty app/src/features/ directory shows the intended extraction was never done. The moves tables can't be reused by any other page.
findings.suggestion: Move moveTable/loadMoveRows/STAT_LABELS and the evolution-tree helpers into src/features/moves.js and src/components or lib/, leaving the route to fetch and forward props.

findings.issue: Client scripts are coupled to server-rendered markup through unowned string literals ('home-search', 'home-results', 'pokemon-game', 'data-sort-value'), and the pervasive optional chaining means a rename in the server template silently kills live filtering or sorting instead of erroring.
findings.suggestion: Define the IDs and data-* attribute names once (a shared constants module imported by both the route and its .client.js, or at least a comment at each end naming its counterpart).

findings.issue: Dead code: sortSpeciesById is exported but never called; app/src/features/ is an empty directory. Both suggest abandoned scaffolding that misleads readers about where code lives.
findings.suggestion: Delete the unused export and the empty directory (or fill the directory by moving the move-table/evolution helpers there, per finding 3).

findings.issue: The '– Pokédex' title suffix is hand-built in six handlers (also (home).js:84, types/index.js:23, moves/[name].js:38, types/[name].js:60, pokemon/[name].js:255, 404.js:8), duplicating the spec's title rule per page.
findings.suggestion: Let document.js derive the document title from a single h1/pageTitle value, or provide a pageTitle(name) helper, so the format is defined once.

findings.issue: The call site wraps type.data.pokemon entries in {pokemon: entry.pokemon} solely to satisfy uniqueSpeciesFromPokemonReferences, which itself accepts two shapes (entry.pokemon?.url ?? entry.url, api.js:230) — a mild dual-shape/flag seam that every new caller has to puzzle out.
findings.suggestion: Have the helper accept a plain list of {url} or {pokemon} entries and normalize explicitly at the boundary, or add a thin speciesFromTypeEntries/type-specific wrapper so the shape contract is obvious.

findings.issue: Error branches re-declare the entire empty prop shape by hand ((home).js:100-112, types/index.js:24-27), so adding a prop means remembering to update the failure path too or the template's destructuring defaults mask the drift.
findings.suggestion: Build the props object once with defaults and merge over it, or have the template fall back on a single shared empty-state shape.

findings.issue: All styling lives in one 588-line global stylesheet keyed by page-specific class names, so removing a feature (e.g. .hidden-ability, .move-summary, .type-grid) requires grepping the global file and reliably leaves dead rules behind.
findings.suggestion: Split per-route rules into co-located .css files (Gracile treats sibling stylesheets as route assets and ignores them for routing) or at least group them under feature comments so deletions are mechanical.

findings.issue: The stylesheet href uses new URL('./document.css', import.meta.url).pathname — a non-obvious trick that happens to be rewritten by Vite's build (verified in dist/server/entrypoint.js) but reads like a bug and is undocumented in the framework docs, which recommend root-relative paths like /src/styles/global.css.
findings.suggestion: Switch to the documented '/src/document.css' form, or add a comment explaining that the FS-absolute path is intentionally resolved/rewritten by the build.

summary: This is idiomatic current-release Gracile (correct route/defineRoute/document/handler shape, the documented Express adapter, co-located .client.js islands) with a genuinely good data layer: one module owns the API base URL, caching and media URLs, and one shared pokemonCard component covers every card list, so data-source changes and sprite-class bugs are one-file fixes. The weakness is the route layer: the undocumented GRACILE_BUILD build guard and the 404 handling are copy-pasted across five or six files, and the Pokémon route is a 360-line monolith holding the whole Moves subsystem, with an empty src/features/ directory hinting at an extraction that never happened. Net: comfortably maintainable, but new pages are copies rather than reuse, and a maintainer must rediscover two non-obvious tricks (the build guard and the stylesheet URL) on their own.
